mainTopic: Shared עירוב problems for courtyards and houses that open one into another: forgotten contributors, ביטול רשות, single residents, a גוי, and passageway houses (בית שער).
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא about two courtyards, one inside the other, that share one עירוב when one resident forgets to join. רבי עקיבא forbids both courtyards in every case. The חכמים permit the inner courtyard when the עירוב is inside and the one who forgot lives outside. Through a series of questions and answers, the גמרא shows that רבי עקיבא allows ביטול רשות between courtyards and the חכמים do not. It then shows that the argument between שמואל and רבי יוחנן need not match this dispute. Next comes the case of courtyards with single residents. רב יוסף's report is corrected by רב ביבי, and שמואל gives a more lenient rule. רבי אלעזר adds that a גוי counts like many people. Finally, שמואל and רבי יוחנן argue whether a passageway used by one person counts as a בית שער, and רב introduces a case of two courtyards with three houses between them, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the earlier statement: רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support. In it, רבי עקיבא rules that whenever one resident forgets to join the shared עירוב, both courtyards are forbidden, no matter where the עירוב was placed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: If they put their עירוב in the outer courtyard and one person forgot to join, whether from the outer or the inner courtyard, both courtyards are forbidden. If they put their עירוב in the inner courtyard and one person from the inner courtyard forgot, both are forbidden. If he was from the outer courtyard, both are still forbidden. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to back up what was just said on the previous amud. The first half gives רבי עקיבא's opinion that both courtyards are forbidden in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two courtyards made one joint עירוב, so they act as one unit. In רבי עקיבא's view, one missing person ruins the עירוב for everyone in both courtyards. This holds whichever courtyard he lives in and wherever the עירוב was placed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way. Introduces a ברייתא that supports a statement.
Shared food that joins residents so they may carry together on שבת
The outer courtyard, which the inner residents pass through
The inner courtyard, whose residents exit only through the outer one
Both courtyards are forbidden for carrying

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the picture clear: the inner courtyard has no exit of its own. Its residents walk through the outer courtyard. That is why the two courtyards are linked.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
If they placed their eiruv in the outer courtyard,
and one person forgot,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין מִן הַחִיצוֹנָה וּבֵין מִן הַפְּנִימִית,
phrases.english: whether from the outer or from the inner courtyard,
and did not join the eiruv, both are forbidden.
If they placed their eiruv in the inner courtyard,
and one from the inner courtyard forgot
and did not join, both are forbidden.
If one from the outer courtyard did not join,
both are forbidden.
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the statement made on the previous amud.
steps.raayaObject: The earlier claim that this case is a dispute between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים

steps.title: The חכמים permit the inner courtyard in one case
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree in one case. If the עירוב was in the inner courtyard and the one who forgot lives in the outer courtyard, the inner courtyard is permitted and the outer one is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: In this case, the inner courtyard is permitted and the outer one is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the opinion of the חכמים, who argue with רבי עקיבא about one specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בזו means 'in this case.' It points to the last case: the עירוב is in the inner courtyard and an outer resident forgot. In every other case the חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא that both courtyards are forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya tries to explain why the inner courtyard is permitted here according to the חכמים but not according to רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
In this case, the inner courtyard is permitted
and the outer one is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the עירוב is in the inner courtyard and an outer resident forgot, the inner courtyard is permitted and the outer one is forbidden.

steps.title: Why can't the inner courtyard just close its door for רבי עקיבא too?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חנן asks אביי a question. The חכמים permit the inner courtyard because its residents can close their door and use the courtyard alone. So why can't they do the same according to רבי עקיבא?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חנן said to אביי: Why do the חכמים say the inner courtyard is permitted? Because the inner residents can close the door and use their courtyard alone. Then according to רבי עקיבא too, let them close the door and use it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר חנן challenges רבי עקיבא's ruling. The reasoning that works for the חכמים seems like it should work for him too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumed reason for the חכמים is simple. The inner residents can lock out the outer courtyard, and then the person who forgot no longer bothers them. That logic seems to have nothing to do with the dispute, so why would רבי עקיבא reject it?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabba bar Chanan said to Abaye:
What is different according to the Rabbis,
who say the inner courtyard is permitted?
Because it can close the door and use its courtyard.
According to Rabbi Akiva as well,
let it close the door and use it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה בַּר חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי: מַאי שְׁנָא לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning behind the dispute in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that the inner courtyard is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'close the door' reasoning used by the חכמים should apply equally for רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: אביי: the עירוב gets people used to coming in
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that closing the door does not help for רבי עקיבא. Because the עירוב sits in the inner courtyard, the outer residents are used to coming in.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The עירוב makes them used to it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבה בר חנן with a reason why the door solution fails according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The outer residents have a share in the עירוב, which is kept in the inner courtyard. So they are used to walking in there. A closed door will not really stop them, and they keep their connection to the inner courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes her accustomed. The outer residents become used to entering.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The eiruv makes them accustomed to come in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical reason the proposed solution does not work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Closing the door cuts the outer courtyard off for both opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the עירוב sits inside, the outer residents are used to entering, so closing the door is not enough.

steps.title: But the עירוב is in the inner courtyard for the חכמים too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The עירוב sits in the inner courtyard according to the חכמים as well, so the outer residents should be used to entering for them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the חכמים too, the עירוב makes them used to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer. His reason seems to apply just as well to the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If עירוב מרגילה makes the inner courtyard forbidden for רבי עקיבא, it should do the same for the חכמים. Then nothing explains why the חכמים permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the Rabbis as well

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis too, the eiruv makes them accustomed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason applies to both opinions, so it cannot explain the difference between them.

steps.title: The inner courtyard says: we joined you to help, not to hurt
steps.stepSummary: According to the חכמים, the inner residents can tell the outer residents: 'We partnered with you for our benefit, not our harm.' Once someone forgot and the partnership hurts them, they may cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the inner courtyard can say: 'I joined with you to improve things, not to ruin them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for the חכמים. The inner residents can back out of the partnership once it starts to harm them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining the עירוב was meant to help the inner residents. Now that the forgetful outer resident would make them forbidden, they can say the deal does not hold when it works against them. So for the חכמים, the habit of coming in (מרגילה) no longer matters.
steps.confusionAlert: דאמרה means 'she says.' The 'she' is the courtyard (חצר is feminine), meaning the residents of the inner courtyard.

phrases.english: Because it (the inner courtyard) says: I partnered with you to improve,
and not to ruin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a separate reason that applies to the חכמים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The habit of entering forbids the inner courtyard for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the חכמים, the inner residents may cancel a partnership that harms them.

steps.title: Why can't the inner courtyard say this for רבי עקיבא too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the inner residents cannot use the same claim, 'we joined to help, not to hurt,' according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא too, let it say: 'I joined with you to improve things, not to ruin them!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. The 'we joined to help, not to hurt' claim seems like it should work for רבי עקיבא as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in this claim seems tied to either opinion. If it frees the inner courtyard for the חכמים, why not for רבי עקיבא?

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Akiva too, let it say:
I partnered with you to improve, and not to ruin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 6 back against רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that the inner courtyard is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The partnership-cancellation claim should free the inner courtyard for רבי עקיבא too.

steps.title: For רבי עקיבא, the outer courtyard can give up its rights
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי עקיבא there is a different fix. The outer courtyard can say 'we give up our rights to you,' and then the inner courtyard becomes permitted. His 'forbidden' ruling applies only before that happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the outer courtyard can say to it: 'We give up our rights to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא does not need the 'cancel the partnership' claim. He has another solution: the outer residents can give up their rights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the outer residents can do ביטול רשות in favor of the inner courtyard. That solves the problem, so the inner courtyard is not stuck. When he says 'both are forbidden,' he means before any such ביטול.
steps.confusionAlert: Here דאמרה לה means the outer courtyard is speaking to the inner one. In step 6 it was the inner courtyard speaking.

phrases.english: Because it (the outer courtyard) says to it: We renounce our rights to you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits רבי עקיבא's ruling to the time before a ביטול רשות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא leaves the inner courtyard forbidden with no way out.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא, the outer residents can give up their rights, which makes the inner courtyard permitted.

steps.title: The חכמים: no giving up rights from one courtyard to another
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that ביטול רשות does not work from one courtyard to another. That is why they need the 'we joined to help, not to hurt' claim to permit the inner courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים hold: there is no giving up of rights from one courtyard to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the explanation by stating the root disagreement. רבי עקיבא allows ביטול רשות between courtyards, and the חכמים do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why each side uses a different tool. רבי עקיבא can rely on ביטול רשות, so he has no need to let the inner courtyard cancel the partnership. The חכמים reject ביטול רשות between courtyards, so they rely on the partnership-cancellation claim instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Giving up one's rights in a shared area so others may carry

steps.whatToRemember: There are three steps of reasoning. (1) For רבי עקיבא, closing the door does not help, because עירוב מרגילה. (2) The חכמים permit the inner courtyard because it can say לתקוני שיתפתיך ולא לעוותי. (3) רבי עקיבא doesn't need that claim, since the outer courtyard can do ביטול רשות. The חכמים hold אין ביטול רשות מחצר לחצר.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן, אֵין בִּיטּוּל רְשׁוּת מֵחָצֵר לְחָצֵר.
phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold: there is no renunciation of rights from courtyard to courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, אֵין בִּיטּוּל רְשׁוּת מֵחָצֵר לְחָצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the חכמים do not use the step 8 solution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the underlying disagreement between the two views
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים could also use ביטול רשות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים reject ביטול רשות between courtyards, so they rely on לתקוני שיתפתיך.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute comes down to whether ביטול רשות works between two courtyards: רבי עקיבא says yes, and the חכמים say no.

steps.title: Is the שמואל and רבי יוחנן dispute the same as this one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל agrees with the חכמים and רבי יוחנן agrees with רבי עקיבא on whether ביטול רשות works between courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that שמואל and רבי יוחנן argue about the same thing that the חכמים and רבי עקיבא argue about? שמואל would agree with the חכמים, and רבי יוחנן would agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to link two disputes. It proposes that שמואל and רבי יוחנן are simply repeating the argument between the חכמים and רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 showed that the חכמים hold that ביטול רשות does not work from one courtyard to another, which seems to imply that רבי עקיבא holds it does. שמואל says it does not work, and רבי יוחנן says it does. So the גמרא suggests their argument is just the older dispute between the תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggested link that may be rejected)

phrases.english: Shall we say that Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבָּנַן וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: disagree about the dispute of the Rabbis and Rabbi Akiva?
So Shmuel ruled like the Rabbis (renunciation does not work between courtyards),
and Rabbi Yochanan ruled like Rabbi Akiva (renunciation works)?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא שְׁמוּאֵל וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבָּנַן וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Steps 8 and 9, which showed the חכמים and רבי עקיבא differ about ביטול רשות between courtyards, and links that to an argument between אמוראים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute between שמואל and רבי יוחנן simply the same as the dispute between the חכמים and רבי עקיבא?

steps.title: שמואל's view fits even רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: שמואל can say that רבי עקיבא allows ביטול רשות only where the two courtyards limit each other, which is not true in שמואל's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל could tell you: what I said fits even רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא allowed it only here, with one courtyard inside the other, because they limit each other. But there, in my case, do the courtyards limit each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. It shows that his ruling does not have to go against רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה the inner residents must walk through the outer courtyard, so each courtyard limits the other. Because of that close link, רבי עקיבא allows one courtyard to give its rights to the other. In שמואל's case the courtyards do not limit each other, so even רבי עקיבא could agree that ביטול רשות does not work there.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this far, meaning his ruling is limited to this case
One inside the other (an inner and an outer courtyard)
They forbid carrying for each other

phrases.english: Shmuel could say to you:
What I said holds even according to Rabbi Akiva.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva only said his view here

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת זוֹ לִפְנִים מִזּוֹ,
phrases.english: in the case of two courtyards, one inside the other,
which forbid carrying for each other;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָתָם, מִי קָא אָסְרָן אַהֲדָדֵי?
phrases.english: but there, do they forbid carrying for each other?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ שְׁמוּאֵל: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 10's link for שמואל by showing that רבי עקיבא's case is different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא by case facts)
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא allows ביטול רשות only where the courtyards limit each other, so שמואל's case is different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion in Step 10 that שמואל's ruling follows the חכמים against רבי עקיבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי עקיבא allowed ביטול רשות only for courtyards one inside the other, which forbid each other. שמואל's case of courtyards that do not forbid each other is different, so שמואל need not oppose רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's view fits even the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן can say that the חכמים rejected ביטול רשות only because the outer courtyard was limiting the inner one, which is not true in his case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן could say: what I said fits even the חכמים. They spoke only here, where the inner courtyard tells the outer one: 'Until you give up your rights to me, you keep forbidding me.' But there, does one courtyard forbid the other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן the same way. It shows that his ruling does not have to go against the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה the outer courtyard limits the inner one. So the inner residents prefer to cut the connection completely rather than depend on the outer residents giving up their rights (see Step 6). That is why the חכמים do not use ביטול רשות here. In רבי יוחנן's case nobody limits anybody, so even the חכמים could agree that ביטול רשות works.

keyTerms.meaning: Until you give up your rights to me

steps.whatToRemember: Both אמוראים use the same key difference. In our משנה the courtyards limit each other, but in the earlier case they do not. So the two disputes are not the same.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan could say:
What I said holds even according to the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָכָא,
phrases.english: The Rabbis only said their view here
because the inner courtyard says to the outer one:
'Until you give up your rights to me, you keep forbidding me.'
But there, does one courtyard forbid the other?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 11. This time רבי יוחנן's view is defended against the חכמים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (אוקימתא by case facts)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן goes against the חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים rejected ביטול רשות only where the outer courtyard limits the inner one, so רבי יוחנן's case is different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion in Step 10 that רבי יוחנן's ruling follows רבי עקיבא against the חכמים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חכמים rejected ביטול רשות only because the inner courtyard says 'אדמבטלת לי קא אסרת עלאי'. Where one courtyard does not forbid the other, even the חכמים could accept it, so רבי יוחנן need not oppose them.

steps.title: Three residents in two courtyards are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the משנה's case of courtyards with single residents, רב יוסף reports that רבי taught: if there are three people in total, carrying is forbidden without an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if the courtyards belonged to single residents, and so on.' רב יוסף said that רבי teaches: if there were three people, carrying is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה about courtyards where only one person lives in each. רב יוסף adds a limit: once there are three residents, they need an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says single residents do not need an עירוב. רבי's teaching shows that this applies only to one person in each courtyard. With three people in total, whether two are inside and one outside or the reverse, a group exists, and carrying is forbidden without an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Single residents (one person living in each courtyard)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical limit of the משנה's leniency. Only one person per courtyard is free from needing an עירוב.

phrases.english: The mishna said: 'And if they belonged to single residents, and so on.'
Rav Yosef said: Rabbi taught:
If there were three people, they are forbidden to carry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הָיוּ שֶׁל יְחִידִים וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, תָּנֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If two courtyards, one inside the other, have three residents in total, carrying is forbidden without an עירוב.

steps.title: רב ביבי corrects רב יוסף's report
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי says רב יוסף's version is mistaken. He himself taught it to רב יוסף, in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה, and the reason was that the outer courtyard has 'many' people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי told them: Don't listen to him. I told him this teaching, and I told it in the name of רב אדא בר אהבה. The reason is that I call them 'many' in the outer courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי rejects the version רב יוסף reported in the previous step. He gives the correct source and the correct reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said 'רבי' taught that three people in total forbid carrying. רב ביבי says the real teaching came from רב אדא בר אהבה. It is about the outer courtyard having רבים, two or more people. When the outer courtyard counts as 'many,' the חכמים forbade carrying as a גזירה, a protective decree, so people would not confuse this case with one where the inner courtyard has many people.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't listen to him; his version is wrong

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' (the name of רבי יהודה הנשיא) and 'רבים' (many) look almost the same in writing and sound similar. That similarity is exactly what caused the mistake.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai said to them:
Do not listen to him,
I told it to him,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אַמְרִיתַהּ נִיהֲלֵהּ,
phrases.english: and I told it to him in the name of Rav Adda bar Ahava,
since I call them
"many" in the outer courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects and corrects the report given in Step 13
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The attribution to 'רבי' and the 'three people in total' wording of רב יוסף's report
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יוסף misheard 'רבים' (many) as 'רבי' and attributed the teaching to the wrong person

steps.title: רב יוסף admits he confused two words
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף accepts the correction. He realizes he mixed up 'רבים' and 'רבי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Master of אברהם! I confused 'רבים' with 'רבי'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף admits that רב ביבי is right. This closes the question of what the correct version of the teaching is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף explains how his error happened. He heard 'רבים' (many) and remembered it as 'רבי' (רבי יהודה הנשיא). Once he accepts this, רב ביבי's version stands as the correct one.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of אברהם! An exclamation of surprise or realization
It got switched for me; I confused it

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Master of Abraham!
I confused "many" with "Rabbi."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the correction made in Step 14
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The correct teaching is from רב אדא בר אהבה, about 'many' people in the outer courtyard. It is not from רבי.

steps.title: שמואל: forbidden only when two live in the inner courtyard
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that the courtyards are permitted. The only exception is when two people live in the inner courtyard and one in the outer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: They are always permitted, unless there are two people in the inner courtyard and one in the outer.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different, more lenient rule for the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אדא בר אהבה, having many people in the outer courtyard is enough to forbid carrying. שמואל disagrees. For him, only a crowd in the inner courtyard causes a problem. Several people walking through the outer courtyard on their way out restrict the one person living there. If the outer courtyard has many people and the inner has only one, carrying stays permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: רב אדא בר אהבה forbids carrying when there are many people in the outer courtyard. שמואל forbids it only when there are many people in the inner courtyard.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Actually, they are permitted,
unless there are two in the inner courtyard
and one in the outer one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the corrected teaching of רב אדא בר אהבה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying is forbidden only when two people live in the inner courtyard and one lives in the outer courtyard.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: a gentile counts as many people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that a single גוי counts like 'רבים'. A גוי living in the inner courtyard therefore restricts carrying in the outer courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A גוי is considered like many people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds a new rule. One גוי is treated like a group of people, unlike one Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single Jew in the inner courtyard does not forbid the outer courtyard. A single גוי does, because he counts like 'many.' The next step asks why the two are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: He is considered like many people

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
And a gentile is considered like many.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: וְגוֹי הֲרֵי הוּא כְּרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the idea of 'רבים' and applies it to a גוי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A single גוי counts like many people and restricts carrying.

steps.title: Why should a gentile be different from a single Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר. A single Jew does not forbid because onlookers will assume an עירוב was made. Onlookers could just as easily assume the Jew rented the גוי's rights.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does a single Jew not forbid? Because whoever knows the facts knows them, and whoever doesn't know thinks an עירוב was made. With a גוי we should say the same: whoever knows, knows, and whoever doesn't know thinks the Jew rented from the גוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אלעזר's ruling. It argues that the same reasoning that permits a single Jew should also permit a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one Jew, there is no fear that people will learn the wrong lesson. Anyone unaware of the details will assume an עירוב was made. The same should work for a גוי. Anyone unaware will assume the Jew made a שכירות, a rental of the גוי's rights, which is the proper fix when a גוי lives there. So why should a גוי count as 'many'?

phrases.english: What is different about a Jew, that he does not prohibit?
Because one who knows, knows,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּלָא יָדַע סָבַר: עָירוֹבֵי עָירֵב,
phrases.english: and one who does not know thinks: an eiruv was made.
With a gentile too, let us say:
one who knows, knows,
and one who does not know thinks: he rented it out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling in Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's rule that a גוי counts like many people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reasoning that permits a single Jew (people will assume an עירוב was made) should equally permit a גוי (people will assume a rental was made).

steps.title: A gentile who rented would talk about it
steps.stepSummary: An ordinary גוי who rented out his rights would loudly tell people. Since he is silent, everyone will assume there was no rental.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ordinary גוי, if he had really rented it out, would go around talking about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Onlookers will not assume a rental took place, because a real rental would have become public knowledge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a Jew, it is reasonable for people to quietly assume an עירוב was made. With a גוי, people expect that a rental would be talked about. If they heard nothing, they would conclude there was none. They might then think carrying is allowed even without a rental. That is why a single גוי forbids carrying, like 'many.'

keyTerms.meaning: He would shout about it, make it widely known

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי counts like 'רבים' because people expect any rental from him to be public. Without such news, onlookers would not assume a valid rental took place.

phrases.english: A typical gentile,
if he had really rented it out,
he would chatter about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases based on how people realistically behave
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Onlookers would assume a rental from the גוי, just as they assume an עירוב for a Jew.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי would publicize a rental. His silence signals there was no rental, so the leniency does not apply and he counts like many.

steps.title: Ten houses in a row: only the innermost contributes
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that when ten houses sit one inside the other, only the innermost house gives to the עירוב of the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If there are ten houses, each one further inside than the one before, the innermost house gives its share to the עירוב, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. שמואל rules on a row of houses where the inner people must walk through the outer houses to reach the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person in the innermost house walks through all nine other houses to get out. That makes those nine houses work like a passageway (בית שער) for him. People living in a בית שער do not need to join the עירוב, so only the innermost house contributes.

keyTerms.meaning: One inside the other (in a row, each further in)
Shared food that joins the residents so they may carry in the courtyard on שבת

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Ten houses, one inside the other,
phrases.notes: The innermost resident must pass through all the others to reach the courtyard.

phrases.english: the innermost one gives its eiruv, and that is enough.
phrases.notes: The outer houses count as his passageways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: עֲשָׂרָה בָּתִּים זֶה לִפְנִים מִזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the גוי in the inner courtyard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With ten houses one inside the other, only the innermost house contributes to the עירוב. The rest count as its בית שער.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even the outer one contributes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says even the 'outer' house must contribute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even the outer one gives to the עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different ruling from שמואל. He says the innermost house is not the only one that contributes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance 'the outer one' sounds like the house nearest the courtyard. The next step questions this reading, because that house is clearly a passageway for everyone.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said: Even the outer one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An opposing view to שמואל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An 'outer' house also has to contribute to the עירוב.

steps.title: But the outer house is a gatehouse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the outer house can contribute when it is obviously a passageway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The outer house is a בית שער! Why should it contribute?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן. The outermost house is the passageway that all the inner houses walk through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית שער does not have to give to the עירוב. The outermost house is used as a passageway by all nine inner houses, so it is the clearest example of a בית שער. So 'even the outer one' cannot mean that house.

keyTerms.meaning: Gatehouse, a passageway room. People living there do not need to give to the עירוב

phrases.english: The outer one is a gatehouse!?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the plain reading of רבי יוחנן's word חיצון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The outermost house is a passageway for everyone, so by the בית שער rule it should be exempt.

steps.title: He means the house just outside the innermost one
steps.stepSummary: 'Outer' means the house right next to the innermost one, which is outer only compared to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He meant the house that is 'outer' compared to the innermost one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining which house רבי יוחנן meant. He meant house number nine, the one right outside the innermost house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: House nine is used as a passageway by only one house, the innermost one. רבי יוחנן says this house must also give to the עירוב. Houses one through eight still count as passageways and do not give.

keyTerms.meaning: The house outside the innermost one (house #9)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture the house closest to the courtyard. רבי יוחנן means the second-to-innermost house.

phrases.english: The outer one of the innermost one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by changing which house 'outer' refers to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word (redefining the case)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Outer' meant the outermost house, which is plainly a בית שער.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Outer' means house #9, which only the innermost house walks through.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle שמואל and רבי יוחנן argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind the argument. It is setting up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know exactly which house they argue about, house #9. The גמרא wants the general principle that explains why they rule differently on it.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the case is clear, it asks for the principle behind the argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle dividing שמואל and רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Does a gatehouse for one person count as a gatehouse?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that a passageway for one person counts as a בית שער. רבי יוחנן holds it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master (שמואל) holds that a passageway used by one person is called a בית שער. The other master (רבי יוחנן) holds it is not called a בית שער.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the principle. They argue about whether a passageway used by just one individual counts as a בית שער.
steps.deeperAnalysis: House #9 is a passageway only for the innermost house. שמואל says that is still a בית שער, so house #9 is exempt. רבי יוחנן says a passageway for only one person is not a real בית שער, so house #9 must contribute.

keyTerms.meaning: A gatehouse used by only one individual

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument is about a passageway that serves one person. שמואל says it counts as a בית שער (only the innermost house contributes). רבי יוחנן says it does not (house #9 contributes too).

phrases.english: One master holds: a gatehouse of an individual
is called a gatehouse.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's view: house #9 is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָא שְׁמֵיהּ בֵּית שַׁעַר.
phrases.english: And the other master holds: it is not called a gatehouse.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's view: house #9 must contribute.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: בֵּית שַׁעַר דְּיָחִיד שְׁמֵיהּ בֵּית שַׁעַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree whether a בית שער used by a single individual still has the status of a בית שער.

steps.title: רב's case: two courtyards with three houses between them
steps.stepSummary: רב describes two courtyards with three houses in a row between them. A resident from each side walks through his own house and puts his עירוב in the middle house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה in the name of רב: There are two courtyards with three houses between them. This one (from one courtyard) comes through this house and puts his עירוב in that middle house. And that one (from the other courtyard) comes through this other house and puts his עירוב in that middle house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case from רב. This step only describes the case. The ruling comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture three houses in a row: the first opens to courtyard A, the third opens to courtyard B, and the middle one sits between them. Each courtyard places its עירוב in the same middle house, reaching it through its own side house. The question of what this does to each courtyard is about to be answered.

keyTerms.meaning: This one comes by way of this (house)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
Two courtyards and three houses between them,
this one comes by way of this (house),
phrases.notes: A resident of courtyard A walks through the house opening to his courtyard.

phrases.english: and places his eiruv in this (middle house).
phrases.notes: Don't stop here; the case is still being set up.

phrases.english: And this one comes by way of this (other house),
phrases.notes: A resident of courtyard B walks through the house opening to his courtyard.

phrases.english: and places his eiruv in this (middle house).
phrases.notes: The ruling follows on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב: שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת וּשְׁלֹשָׁה בָּתִּים בֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case, related to the theme of houses that serve as passageways.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup only: two courtyards each place an עירוב in the shared middle house. The ruling continues on the next amud.
